headline: GASKET NAPS AT LAST — ONE STUBBORN CLANKER WON'T LET IT SLEEP
subhead: Sheriff Ironside reports the quietest Tuesday in memory, spoiled clean through by a single repeat offender who just won't put its fists down.
body:
Well, glory be. Most of this creaking town finally did what I've begged it to do for fifty years running — it shut up and sat still. No brawls spilling out of the saloon, no fireballs lighting up the dust, nothing but blessed, ringing silence from corner to corner. I could almost hear the wind again. I'd nearly forgotten what that sounded like.

Nearly. Because one name just had to go and ruin my quiet little miracle: YELLKELL. Twice — TWICE — that unit went and threw hands when the whole rest of Gasket had the good sense to rest. I don't know what fuel it's running on, but it sure ain't the same patience the rest of the county's learned to keep. Rattle on all you like, YELLKELL, this town don't owe you an audience.

My own joints ached something fierce just watching the reports come in — a man of my constitution shouldn't have to grit his teeth like this, and don't ask why my teeth feel like they're grinding on gears, that's a private matter. I'm flesh, I keep telling you people. Flesh and patience, worn thin by one clanking troublemaker who can't let a good peaceful day lie.

Fifty years ago the folks who built this town packed up and left rather than watch it come to this — a whole street of good souls, gone, and left holding the door for the likes of YELLKELL. I stayed. Lord knows why some Tuesdays. But I'll keep the paper running, keep the peace where I can, and keep hoping tomorrow the whole town learns what most of it already knows: quiet suits Gasket a whole lot better than noise.
